question: Does a bounded Legendre-character basis remove the apparent prime full-support RS interval-search advantage?
input_model: odd prime p, explicit block length N=p, H_d[j,x]=x^j on all x=0..p-1, arbitrary public target syndrome or particular word, 1<=d<=(p-1)/2
mechanism: closed-form inverse coordinates in the constant plus p-1 shifted character lattice basis; exact unbiased random rounding OR deterministic integer-potential conditional expectations; native residual verification
deterministic_guarantee: uniform all-target search when the exact rational-log Hoeffding potential certificate is <1; O(sqrt(p log p)) certified width, no random coin premise
deterministic_cost: O(p^2) operations on O(p log p)-bit integers; O(p^2 log p) bits working storage
classical_guarantee: uniform all-target per-attempt failure <= min(1, 2p exp(-2(u+1)^2/p)); full interval has zero failure; integer dyadic outward certificates
complexity: O(p^2) O(log p)-bit integer arithmetic per attempt and O(p) streamed working storage; syndrome preparation additionally O(d^3) field operations; expected <=2 attempts at certified_radius(p)=O(sqrt(p log p))
quantum_advantage: none claimed; attacks the support-search task rather than compiling the conditional quantum receiver
proof_obligations: native character polynomial moment identity and sharp half-rate boundary
full real rank, Gram identity and determinant p^((p-1)/2)
exact coordinate reconstruction and correct signed unbiased rounding
fresh independent coins, integer residual threshold and column union bound
deterministic alternative: exact common-denominator potential factors, conditional branch identity, monotonicity, rational log enclosures, final residual potential replay
unchanged targets, all failed rounds retained, original modular and polynomial witness replay
independent research review and prior-art comparison before any novelty claim
falsifiers: a row outside the claimed native kernel or failure of the character Gram inverse
a biased signed-numerator rounding distribution or a raw residual with nonzero mean
an accepted witness failing native moments, interval membership or polynomial replay
an attempt to extrapolate the bound to d>(p-1)/2, arbitrary acceptance sets, prescribed sampling, or punctured exponentially large fields
experiments: independent exact Gram/determinant/inverse and next-moment controls
exhaustive small exact rounding distributions and all small syndromes
same-target replay of the 24 prior LLL interval records
half-rate p257/509/1021 with declared certified widths and public targets
impossible zero-width nonzero-syndrome control with all failed rounds retained
independent exhaustive small conditional expectations, permitted-branch greedy choices and naive-nearest linear-error spike falsifier
